title: Exemplar routing sandbox
body:
Notes to self: 

Purpose: quick scratchpad for experimenting with exemplar routing strategies for few-shot prompts. Goal is to find practical heuristics that (a) improve output fidelity on classification-like tasks, (b) avoid large token overhead, and (c) degrade gracefully when exemplars are noisy.

High-level ideas to test:
- Dynamic exemplar selection by cosine similarity of query embedding to candidate exemplars (baseline).
- Routing by cluster centroid with exemplar diversity constraint (max 1 high-sim exemplar per cluster).
- Time-aware routing: prefer recent exemplars for user-personalization tasks, fallback to canonical exemplars otherwise.
- Heuristic hybrid: top-K embedding similarity but then dedupe by semantic-role (intent/slot) labels when available.
- Budgeted exemplar packs: limit by token budget; pack highest marginal utility exemplars using greedy submodular selection.

Quick experiments I want to run locally (small test harness):
- Dataset: internal "support-utterance-intent-5000" subset (balanced across 8 intents). Keep 800 holdout queries.
- Exemplar pool: 1200 candidate exemplars (variety of phrasings). Precompute embeddings (text-embedding-001-like).
- Metrics: top-1 accuracy of model completion into canonical label token, avg token overhead, latency delta (sim + prompt construction), failure modes (hallucination, label drift).

Initial heuristics and example prompt shells:
- Baseline (static 5-shot): 
  System: "You are an intent classifier. Given a user utterance, output exactly one label from the set {billing, cancel, setup, troubleshoot, upgrade, feature, account, other}. No explanation."
  Shots: fixed curated 5 exemplars (high-quality).

- Embedding-topK (dynamic): 
  Steps: compute query embedding q; retrieve top-4 exemplars by cosine; if total token length > 1200 reduce by removing lowest similarity exemplar until under budget; assemble 4-shot prompt.

- Diversity-clustered topK: 
  Steps: pre-cluster exemplar pool into 12 clusters (kmeans on embeddings); select cluster centroids most similar to q, sample 1 exemplar from each until K satisfied; prefer high-confidence labeled exemplars.

Failure cases observed in quick manual runs (notes):
- Near-duplicate exemplars with slightly different labels cause the model to flip between two labels unpredictably. Example: "I need to stop my subscription" vs "I want to cancel" — both mapped to cancel usually, but phrasing with "stop" occasionally predicted "billing" on a few random seeds.
- Token budget trimming by similarity tends to drop the most diverse exemplar, reducing coverage. Need a selection objective that accounts for marginal information.
- Embedding similarity retrieves paraphrases that are semantically close but differ in instructive polarity (e.g., question vs. complaint) which can shift outputs.

Hypotheses to validate: 
1) Greedy submodular selection that maximizes marginal label entropy coverage will outperform top-K similarity for rare intents (esp. "upgrade", "feature").
2) Adding a short role tag before each exemplar ("USER: ...\nLABEL: ...") reduces label drift by clarifying structure.
3) A compact serialized context: instead of full exemplar text, use 1–2 sentence paraphrase + label will keep token cost low with similar accuracy.

Micro-probes and templates to use in evaluation harness: 
- Template A (full exemplar): 
  "USER: {utterance}\nLABEL: {label}\n---"
- Template B (compact paraphrase): 
  "EX: {paraphrase}\nL: {label}\n---"
- Template C (role-anchored): 
  "Example:\n  USER: {utterance}\n  INTENT: {label}\n  >>>"

Notes on noisy exemplars:
- Mark exemplars with a quality score (0–1). Weight retrieval by (similarity * quality). Might help filter crowd-labeled examples.
- Heuristic: if exemplar label has disagreement_count > 1, tag as low-quality and deprioritize.

Edge-case routing rules to implement quickly: 
- If top-1 similarity < T1 (e.g., 0.25) and top-5 similarity spread < delta, then fallback to static canonical 3-shot to avoid garbage retrieval.
- If query length > 300 tokens, force exemplar count to 2 (to keep prompt manageable).
- For personalizable workflows (user id available), include 1 recent user exemplar (if exists) + 3 canonical exemplars.

Logging/observability notes (for future Console integration):
- Log chosen exemplar ids, per-exemplar similarity, and quality score. Compute per-query "exemplar-confidence" metric = mean(similarity*quality). Store with prediction for offline analysis.
- Surface common failure bundles: examples where model label != gold and exemplar-confidence high (this suggests labeling or exemplar mismatch).

Quick pseudo-workflow to implement in the playbook: 
1) Precompute embeddings and quality metadata for exemplar pool.
2) Implement selection strategies as modular policies: topk, cluster, greedy-submodular, hybrid.
3) Small A/B on holdout batch: measure accuracy/token overhead.
4) Triage failure clusters and adjust selection heuristics or curate exemplar pool.

To-dos (short):
- [ ] Implement greedy marginal utility selector (start with label-coverage scoring).
- [ ] Add quality-weighting to retrieval score.
- [ ] Build minimalist logging wrapper for exemplar metadata output.
- [ ] Run experiments on 800-holdout described above and collect results.
- [ ] Draft a short doc for Console metrics to propose: exemplar-confidence, exemplar-token-cost, exemplar-hit-rate.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How sensitive are large LLMs (gpt-like) vs distilled/open models to exemplar ordering? Earlier notes show some models are highly order-sensitive; need to test ordering ablations across model candidates.
- Is submodular greedy selection computationally tractable for large pools (50k+ exemplars) in production? Likely need approximation / prefiltering.
- Best way to represent paraphrases compactly? Learn a paraphrase distillation model to compress exemplar into 1–2 canonical lines? Could be a follow-up Research spike.

Random examples and quick manual checks (raw):
- Query: "How do I turn off auto renew?" 
  Top candidates: "I want to cancel subscription", "How do I stop recurring payments?" (labels: cancel, cancel) -> OK
- Query: "My app crashes on login after update" 
  Top candidates: "App crashes after update" (troubleshoot), "Login failing after patch" (troubleshoot) -> both good, but sometimes model outputs "feature" when exemplar phrasing mentions "update" without "crash".

Short retrospective thought: exemplar routing feels like a band-aid for small-shot coverage gaps. Real long-term solution is a hybrid of (1) stronger canonical instruction + (2) lightweight retrieval when really needed. But retrieval might shine when we want personalization or long-tail phrasing coverage.

References and quick links for follow-ups: 
- Slack: #prompt-infra (thread: exemplar-retrieval-discussions)
- Linear: PR-948 (experiment track)
- GH: prompt-playground experiments branch (see linked PR above)

End of scratchpad.

Notes to self: when this stabilizes, convert to a short internal howto for Solutions Eng with a checklist: "when to use dynamic exemplars vs static shots" and provide default params. Keep token budgets as primary constraint.
